title: Physics queries can end up using stale shape data when physics server runs on separate thread
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in : 4.4.1, 4.5 beta1, 4.5 beta2, 4.5 beta 3

### System information

Godot v4.5.beta4 - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7283) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-6700 CPU @ 3.40GHz (8 threads) - 15.90 GiB memory

### Issue description

Using a SphereShape3D or CapsuleShape3D to create a trace using the `collide_shape` method doesn't seem to work and returns these errors (see below). It is supposed to return the hit result position. Here's the function : 

```gdscript
func sphere_trace(pos1: Vector3, radius: float):
	var shape = SphereShape3D.new()
	shape.radius = radius

	var params = PhysicsShapeQueryParameters3D.new()
	params.shape = shape
	params.transform.origin = pos1
	params.collision_mask = (1 << 0) | (1 << 1) | (0 << 2) # Collide with 1 and 2 but not 3

	var result = get_world_3d().direct_space_state.collide_shape(params, 1)

	return result[0] if result.size() > 0 else {}
```

Errors : 
```error
E 0:00:01:253   Script.gd:606 @ spheretrace(): Failed to build Jolt Physics sphere shape with {radius=0.500000}. Its radius must be greater than 0. This shape belongs to '<unknown>' and 0 other object(s).
  <C++ Error>   Condition "radius <= 0.0f" is true. Returning: nullptr
  <C++ Source>  modules/jolt_physics/shapes/jolt_sphere_shape_3d.cpp:38 @ _build()
```
```error
E 0:00:01:239   Script.gd:606 @ spheretrace(): Parameter "jolt_shape" is null.
  <C++ Source>  modules/jolt_physics/spaces/jolt_physics_direct_space_state_3d.cpp:668 @ collide_shape()
```

With the line 606 corresponding to this : 
```gdscript
var result = get_world_3d().direct_space_state.collide_shape(params, 1)
```

### Steps to reproduce

Function : 
```gdscript
func sphere_trace(pos1: Vector3, radius: float):
	var shape = SphereShape3D.new()
	shape.radius = radius

	var params = PhysicsShapeQueryParameters3D.new()
	params.shape = shape
	params.transform.origin = pos1
	params.collision_mask = (1 << 0) | (1 << 1) | (0 << 2) # Collide with 1 and 2 but not 3

	var result = get_world_3d().direct_space_state.collide_shape(params, 1)

	return result[0] if result.size() > 0 else {}
```
